```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tessier_2016_drugS"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tessier_2016_drugS"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12054> (open access, PMC4807465)

Tessier 2016 is a simulation study of the power of pharmacogenetic tests when
phase I data are analysed together with sparse phase II data. Every result in
the paper is simulated from one population PK model: the model estimated from
the phase I data of an oral drug of the Institut de Recherches Servier,
anonymised as "drug S". That model is what this package provides. The
pharmacogenetic part of the paper (simulated SNP effects on clearance, Lasso
and stepwise association tests) is a property of each simulated dataset, not
of the drug, and is described at the end of this article rather than built
into the model.

The authors' simulation code (Supporting Information, Data S1, written in R)
is published with the paper. It contains a closed-form solution of the model
for a single dose and for steady state, which this article uses as an
independent check of the packaged ODE model.

# Population

The model was estimated from drug S concentrations in 78 subjects from three
phase I studies, each given one oral dose of 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 400 or
800 units (6, 6, 24, 12, 12, 6, 6 and 6 subjects) and sampled 16 times between
0.5 and 192 h. All subjects were genotyped at baseline for 176 SNPs on a DNA
microarray of genes involved in drug PK. The paper reports no demographics,
does not say whether the subjects were healthy volunteers, and does not name
the drug or its dose and volume units (Tessier 2016 Methods, "Simulation
study" and "Simulated designs and analysis scenarios"; the population PK
analysis itself was presented as Tessier 2013, PAGE abstract 2836).

The paper's phase II studies (306 subjects, 20, 50 or 100 units once daily,
sampled at steady state) are simulated designs, not observed data.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tessier_2016_drugS"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL) | 94.9 | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (V1) | 1520 | Table 1 |
| `lq` (Q) | 147 | Table 1 |
| `lvp` (V2) | 2130 | Table 1 |
| `ld1` (Tk0) | 1.59 h | Table 1 |
| `ltlag` (Tlag1, zero-order route) | 0.401 h | Table 1; Data S1 `LagTk0` |
| `lka` (Ka) | 0.203 /h | Table 1 |
| `ltlag2` (Tlag2, first-order route) | 22.7 h | Table 1; Data S1 `LagKa` |
| `lemax_ffo` (EmaxFRAC) | 0.45 | Table 1 |
| `ld50_ffo` (D50FRAC) | 18.6 units | Table 1 |
| `lfdepot` (F at or below 20 units) | 1, fixed | Table 1 footnote |
| `limax_fdepot` (ImaxF) | 0.8 | Table 1 |
| `ld50_fdepot` (D50F) | 41.7 units | Table 1 |
| `etalfdepot` | 0.329^2 | Table 1 'omega (%)' 32.9 on F; Data S1 `omF` |
| `etald1` | 0.316^2 | Table 1 31.6; Data S1 `omTk0` |
| `etaltlag` | 0.351^2 | Table 1 35.1; Data S1 `omLagTk0` |
| `etalq` | 0.899^2 | Table 1 89.9; Data S1 `omQ` |
| `etalvp` | 0.442^2 | Table 1 44.2; Data S1 `omV2` |
| `etalcl` | 0.251^2 | Table 1 25.1; Methods 'omega2 CL = 0.06' |
| `propSd` | 0.20 | Table 1 'sigma slope (%)' 20; Data S1 `SIG_slope` |
| `ffo = emax_ffo * DOSE / (d50_ffo + DOSE)` | | Table 1 footnote equation for FRAC |
| `F = 1 - imax_fdepot * (DOSE - 20) / (d50_fdepot + DOSE - 20)`, F = 1 at or below 20 units | | Table 1 footnote equation for F; Data S1 `Fpop` |
| Two-compartment disposition, zero-order input of (1 - FRAC) F DOSE into V1 after Tlag1, first-order input of FRAC F DOSE after Tlag2 | | Supplementary Figure S4; Data S1 closed-form solution |
| `Cc = 1000 * central / vc` | | Data S1 doses `1000 x DOSE` and divides by V1 |

# Dose-dependent absorption

The fraction absorbed by the slow first-order route rises with dose towards
45%, and the bioavailability falls above 20 units towards 20% of its
low-dose value. Both are evaluated from the dose of the administration, which
the model takes as the covariate `DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS`.

```{r dose-terms}
doses <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800)
dose_terms <- tibble(
  dose = doses,
  ffo = 0.45 * dose / (18.6 + dose),
  fdepot = ifelse(dose <= 20, 1, 1 - 0.8 * (dose - 20) / (41.7 + dose - 20))
)
dose_terms |>
  mutate(across(c(ffo, fdepot), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Dose (units)" = dose,
    "First-order fraction FRAC" = ffo,
    "Bioavailability F" = fdepot
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical dose-dependent absorption terms (Table 1 footnote equations).")
```

# Event tables

Each administration is two dose records with the same amount: one into
`depot` for the first-order route and one into `central` with `rate = -2`,
which makes rxode2 use the modelled zero-order duration `dur(central)`. This is
how the authors coded their Monolix dataset (Data S1: two dosing lines per
subject, `RATE = -2` on the zero-order line). The dose covariate is carried on
every row.

```{r events-helpers}
# One single-dose subject block: two dose records plus observations.
single_dose_events <- function(id, dose, obs_times) {
  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      id = id, time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L,
      cmt = c("depot", "central"), rate = c(0, -2)
    ),
    tibble(id = id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS = dose)
}

# Once-daily dosing: n_doses administrations, the last one at time
# (n_doses - 1) * tau, observations at obs_after hours after the last dose.
repeat_dose_events <- function(id, dose, n_doses, obs_after, tau = 24) {
  dose_times <- (seq_len(n_doses) - 1) * tau
  last_dose <- max(dose_times)
  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      id = id, time = rep(dose_times, each = 2), amt = dose, evid = 1L,
      cmt = rep(c("depot", "central"), times = n_doses),
      rate = rep(c(0, -2), times = n_doses)
    ),
    tibble(id = id, time = last_dose + obs_after, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS = dose, last_dose = last_dose)
}
```

# Check against the authors' closed-form solution

Data S1 computes every simulated concentration from a closed-form solution of
the two-compartment model with a lagged zero-order input and a lagged
first-order input, both for a single dose and at steady state under once-daily
dosing. The functions below are those formulas, transcribed from Data S1 with
the same variable names. Because both sides use the same parameters, the
difference between them is pure numerical error, and the checks are tight.

```{r closed-form}
# Data S1 'PK profiles for subjects from phase I study': single dose at time 0.
# DOSE is in the paper's units; Data S1 doses 1000 x DOSE.
cf_single <- function(t, DOSE, F1, CL = 94.9, V1 = 1520, Q = 147, V2 = 2130,
                      Ka = 0.203, Tk0 = 1.59, Lag.Tk0 = 0.401, Lag.Ka = 22.7) {
  FRAC <- 0.45 * DOSE / (18.6 + DOSE)
  D <- 1000 * DOSE
  beta <- 0.5 * ((Q / V1) + (Q / V2) + (CL / V1) -
    sqrt(((Q / V1) + (Q / V2) + (CL / V1))^2 - 4 * (Q / V2) * (CL / V1)))
  alpha <- ((Q / V2) * (CL / V1)) / beta
  A0 <- (1 / V1) * ((alpha - (Q / V2)) / (alpha - beta))
  B0 <- (1 / V1) * ((beta - (Q / V2)) / (beta - alpha))
  A1 <- (Ka / V1) * (((Q / V2) - alpha) / ((Ka - alpha) * (beta - alpha)))
  B1 <- (Ka / V1) * (((Q / V2) - beta) / ((Ka - beta) * (alpha - beta)))
  k0 <- F1 * (1 - FRAC) * D / Tk0
  zero <- ifelse(
    t <= Lag.Tk0, 0,
    ifelse(
      t <= Tk0 + Lag.Tk0,
      k0 * ((A0 / alpha) * (1 - exp(-alpha * (t - Lag.Tk0))) +
        (B0 / beta) * (1 - exp(-beta * (t - Lag.Tk0)))),
      k0 * ((A0 / alpha) * (1 - exp(-alpha * Tk0)) * exp(-alpha * (t - Tk0 - Lag.Tk0)) +
        (B0 / beta) * (1 - exp(-beta * Tk0)) * exp(-beta * (t - Tk0 - Lag.Tk0)))
    )
  )
  first <- ifelse(
    t <= Lag.Ka, 0,
    F1 * FRAC * D * (A1 * exp(-alpha * (t - Lag.Ka)) + B1 * exp(-beta * (t - Lag.Ka)) -
      (A1 + B1) * exp(-Ka * (t - Lag.Ka)))
  )
  zero + first
}

# Data S1 'PK profiles for subjects from phase II study': steady state of
# once-daily dosing, t = time after the last dose (no further doses).
cf_ss <- function(t, DOSE, F1, tau = 24, CL = 94.9, V1 = 1520, Q = 147, V2 = 2130,
                  Ka = 0.203, Tk0 = 1.59, Lag.Tk0 = 0.401, Lag.Ka = 22.7) {
  FRAC <- 0.45 * DOSE / (18.6 + DOSE)
  D <- 1000 * DOSE
  beta <- 0.5 * ((Q / V1) + (Q / V2) + (CL / V1) -
    sqrt(((Q / V1) + (Q / V2) + (CL / V1))^2 - 4 * (Q / V2) * (CL / V1)))
  alpha <- ((Q / V2) * (CL / V1)) / beta
  A0 <- (1 / V1) * ((alpha - (Q / V2)) / (alpha - beta))
  B0 <- (1 / V1) * ((beta - (Q / V2)) / (beta - alpha))
  A1 <- (Ka / V1) * (((Q / V2) - alpha) / ((Ka - alpha) * (beta - alpha)))
  B1 <- (Ka / V1) * (((Q / V2) - beta) / ((Ka - beta) * (alpha - beta)))
  k0 <- F1 * (1 - FRAC) * D / Tk0
  ea <- 1 - exp(-alpha * tau)
  eb <- 1 - exp(-beta * tau)
  zero <- ifelse(
    t <= Lag.Tk0,
    k0 * (A0 / alpha * (1 - exp(-alpha * Tk0)) * exp(-alpha * (t + tau - Lag.Tk0 - Tk0)) / ea +
      B0 / beta * (1 - exp(-beta * Tk0)) * exp(-beta * (t + tau - Lag.Tk0 - Tk0)) / eb),
    ifelse(
      t <= Tk0 + Lag.Tk0,
      k0 * (A0 / alpha * ((1 - exp(-alpha * (t - Lag.Tk0))) +
        exp(-alpha * tau) * (1 - exp(-alpha * Tk0)) * exp(-alpha * (t - Lag.Tk0 - Tk0)) / ea) +
        B0 / beta * ((1 - exp(-beta * (t - Lag.Tk0))) +
          exp(-beta * tau) * (1 - exp(-beta * Tk0)) * exp(-beta * (t - Lag.Tk0 - Tk0)) / eb)),
      k0 * (A0 / alpha * (1 - exp(-alpha * Tk0)) * exp(-alpha * (t - Tk0 - Lag.Tk0)) / ea +
        B0 / beta * (1 - exp(-beta * Tk0)) * exp(-beta * (t - Tk0 - Lag.Tk0)) / eb)
    )
  )
  ek <- 1 - exp(-Ka * tau)
  first <- ifelse(
    t < Lag.Ka,
    F1 * FRAC * D * (A1 * exp(-alpha * (t + tau - Lag.Ka)) / ea +
      B1 * exp(-beta * (t + tau - Lag.Ka)) / eb -
      (A1 + B1) * exp(-Ka * (t + tau - Lag.Ka)) / ek),
    F1 * FRAC * D * (A1 * exp(-alpha * (t - Lag.Ka)) / ea +
      B1 * exp(-beta * (t - Lag.Ka)) / eb -
      (A1 + B1) * exp(-Ka * (t - Lag.Ka)) / ek)
  )
  zero + first
}

f_typ <- function(dose) ifelse(dose <= 20, 1, 1 - 0.8 * (dose - 20) / (41.7 + dose - 20))
```

## Typical single-dose profiles

```{r typical-single}
mod <- readModelDb("Tessier_2016_drugS")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

# zeroRe() removes the random effects on purpose; rxode2 warns on every
# multi-subject solve without omega, so muffle that one warning only.
solve_typical <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

t_dense <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.05), seq(4.25, 48, by = 0.25), seq(49, 240, by = 1))))
ev_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), \(i) single_dose_events(i, doses[i], t_dense)))
sim_typ <- solve_typical(
  mod_typ,
  events = ev_typ, keep = "DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame"
)

chk_typ <- sim_typ |>
  mutate(cf = cf_single(time, DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, f_typ(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS))) |>
  group_by(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS) |>
  summarise(max_abs_diff_rel = max(abs(Cc - cf)) / max(cf), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(chk_typ, digits = 12, caption = "ODE vs Data S1 closed form, typical subject, single dose.")
# Same parameters on both sides, so only integration error remains: measured
# about 4e-11 of the peak at these tolerances, so the bound has wide headroom.
stopifnot(all(chk_typ$max_abs_diff_rel < 1e-6))
```

```{r figure-typical, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim_typ |>
  filter(Cc > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS))) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Cc (milliunits/L)", colour = "Dose (units)",
    title = "Typical drug S profiles after one oral dose",
    caption = "The second rise near 23 h is the lagged first-order route (Tlag2 = 22.7 h)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Individual single-dose profiles

The same comparison for a stochastic phase I cohort, feeding each subject's
own parameters (as returned by `rxSolve()`) into the closed form.

```{r phase1-cohort}
t1 <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 192)
dose_alloc <- rep(doses, times = c(6, 6, 24, 12, 12, 6, 6, 6))
ev_p1 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(dose_alloc), \(i) single_dose_events(i, dose_alloc[i], c(0, t1))))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160304)
sim_p1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_p1, keep = "DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS",
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame"
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_p1$Cc), length(unique(sim_p1$id)) == 78L)

chk_ind <- sim_p1 |>
  mutate(cf = cf_single(
    time, DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, fdepot,
    CL = cl, V1 = vc, Q = q, V2 = vp, Ka = ka, Tk0 = d1, Lag.Tk0 = tlag, Lag.Ka = tlag2
  )) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(max_abs_diff_rel = max(abs(Cc - cf)) / max(cf), .groups = "drop")
summary(chk_ind$max_abs_diff_rel)
# Measured at most about 1e-10 of each subject's peak.
stopifnot(all(chk_ind$max_abs_diff_rel < 1e-6))
```

## Steady state under once-daily dosing

The phase II designs sample at steady state of once-daily dosing. The ODE model
reaches it by a 30-day run-in (the typical terminal half-life is about 33 h,
so the 696 h from the first to the last dose is about 21 half-lives). Do not use `ss = 1` / `ss = 2` with this
model: each administration is a split pair of records with a modelled `f()`,
and rxode2's steady-state solver does not support that combination.

```{r typical-ss}
t_after <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.05), seq(4.25, 24, by = 0.25), seq(25, 96, by = 1))))
ev_ss <- bind_rows(lapply(1:3, \(i) repeat_dose_events(i, c(20, 50, 100)[i], 30, t_after)))
sim_ss <- solve_typical(
  mod_typ,
  events = ev_ss, keep = c("DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS", "last_dose"),
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame"
)
chk_ss <- sim_ss |>
  mutate(
    tad = time - last_dose,
    cf = cf_ss(tad, DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, f_typ(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS))
  ) |>
  filter(tad >= 0) |>
  group_by(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS) |>
  summarise(max_abs_diff_rel = max(abs(Cc - cf)) / max(cf), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(chk_ss, digits = 10, caption = "30-day run-in vs Data S1 steady-state closed form, typical subject.")
# The run-in leaves about exp(-696 / 47.6) = 4e-7 of the accumulation short of
# steady state; measured about 2.5e-7 of the peak.
stopifnot(all(chk_ss$max_abs_diff_rel < 1e-5))
```

# Replicate Supplementary Figure S5

Supplementary Figure S5 shows one simulated dataset: the 78 phase I subjects
(16 samples after one dose) and the 306 phase II subjects of design
SPI/II3s.96h (steady state of 20, 50 or 100 units once daily, sampled 2, 22
and 96 h after the last dose; Data S1 `t2`). The figure below is the same
design simulated with residual error, without the SNP effects (they barely
move the profiles at a 25% CL variability, Supplementary Material "Simulated
genetic effects").

```{r phase2-cohort}
dose_p2 <- rep(c(20, 50, 100), each = 102)
ev_p2 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(dose_p2), \(i) {
  repeat_dose_events(100L + i, dose_p2[i], 30, c(2, 22, 96))
}))
sim_p2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_p2, keep = c("DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS", "last_dose"),
  maxsteps = 1e6, returnType = "data.frame"
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_p2$Cc), length(unique(sim_p2$id)) == 306L)
```

```{r figure-s5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
fig_s5 <- bind_rows(
  sim_p1 |> filter(time > 0) |> transmute(study = "Phase I", time, sim),
  sim_p2 |> transmute(study = "Phase II (3s.96h)", time = time - last_dose, sim)
) |>
  filter(sim > 0)
ggplot(fig_s5, aes(time, sim, colour = study)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 192, by = 24)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Phase I" = "#d49a9a", "Phase II (3s.96h)" = "#4f7f72")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Simulated concentration (milliunits/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Simulated phase I and phase II concentrations",
    caption = "Replicates the SPI/II3s.96h panels of Supplementary Figure S5 of Tessier 2016."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The simulated concentrations span the same range as Figure S5: about 1 to
100 in the first day, falling to about 0.01 to 1 at 192 h.

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA results, so the NCA below checks the model against
its own analytic exposure. For an oral dose, AUC from zero to infinity is
`F * DOSE / CL` whatever the shape of the input, so the typical dense
profiles must give `1000 * F(DOSE) * DOSE / 94.9`.

```{r pknca-typical}
nca_typ_conc <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(id = DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, treatment = paste(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, "units")) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
nca_typ_dose <- ev_typ |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot") |>
  mutate(id = DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, treatment = paste(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, "units")) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, amt)
nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_typ_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_typ_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
auc_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_typ) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  mutate(analytic = 1000 * f_typ(id) * id / 94.9, ratio = PPORRES / analytic) |>
  arrange(id) |>
  select(treatment, PPORRES, analytic, ratio)
auc_chk |>
  mutate(ratio = sprintf("%.5f", ratio)) |>
  rename("Dose" = treatment, "PKNCA AUC0-inf" = PPORRES, "1000 F D / CL" = analytic, "Ratio" = ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-subject AUC0-inf: PKNCA vs analytic.")
# Linear-up/log-down trapezoids on a 0.05-1 h grid plus a log-linear tail;
# measured within 0.01% of the analytic value.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_chk$ratio - 1) < 0.01))
```

The dose-normalised exposure is constant up to 20 units and then falls, which is
the less-than-proportional exposure the bioavailability term encodes.

The stochastic phase I cohort, on the paper's 16-sample design, by dose group:

```{r pknca-phase1}
nca_p1_conc <- sim_p1 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, "units")) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
nca_p1_dose <- ev_p1 |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot") |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(DOSE_DRUGS_UNITS, "units")) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, amt)
nca_p1 <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_p1_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_p1_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
as.data.frame(nca_p1) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  mutate(dose = as.numeric(sub(" units", "", treatment))) |>
  arrange(dose) |>
  select(treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life) |>
  rename(
    "Dose" = treatment, "Cmax" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median NCA by dose group, stochastic phase I cohort (78 subjects).")
```

# The pharmacogenetic layer

Under the paper's alternative hypothesis six randomly chosen SNPs act on
log(CL) (Eq. 1), together explaining 30% of the CL variability, with
`RGC` = 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 12% for the six variants. Each effect size follows
from its `RGC` and minor allele frequency `p` (Eq. 2):

`beta_k = sqrt(RGC_k * omega2_CL / (2 p_k (1 - p_k) - RGC_k * 2 p_k (1 - p_k)))`

where `omega2_CL` is the non-genetic variance, `0.7 * 0.251^2 = 0.044`, which
the paper rounds to 0.04. Since the causal SNPs differ in every simulated
dataset, the model carries no SNP covariate. To simulate the paper's H1
scenario, lower `etalcl` to the non-genetic variance and add
`sum(beta_k * SNP_k)` to `log(cl)`; for the "IIV CL = 60%" scenario set
`etalcl` to `0.6^2`:

```{r pg-scenarios}
omega2_ng <- (1 - sum(c(0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.07, 0.12))) * 0.251^2
omega2_ng
stopifnot(abs(omega2_ng - 0.04) < 0.005)
mod_h1 <- mod |> rxode2::ini(etalcl ~ 0.044101)
mod_cl60 <- mod |> rxode2::ini(etalcl ~ 0.36)
```

Supplementary Table S1 lists simulated effect sizes and the genotype-based
typical CL, `94.9 * exp(beta * SNP)`. Recomputing that column from the printed
(two-decimal) betas agrees within the rounding of beta:

```{r table-s1}
s1 <- tribble(
  ~scenario, ~rgc, ~pct, ~beta, ~cl1, ~cl2,
  "SPI", "1%", 0.1, 0.03, 97.8, 100.8,
  "SPI", "1%", 0.5, 0.04, 98.4, 102.1,
  "SPI", "1%", 0.9, 0.10, 104.8, 115.8,
  "SPI", "12%", 0.1, 0.11, 106.0, 118.3,
  "SPI", "12%", 0.5, 0.15, 109.9, 127.4,
  "SPI", "12%", 0.9, 0.35, 135.3, 193.0,
  "SPI/II3s.96h", "1%", 0.1, 0.03, 97.8, 100.8,
  "SPI/II3s.96h", "1%", 0.5, 0.04, 98.6, 102.4,
  "SPI/II3s.96h", "1%", 0.9, 0.11, 106.1, 118.6,
  "SPI/II3s.96h", "12%", 0.1, 0.11, 106.0, 118.3,
  "SPI/II3s.96h", "12%", 0.5, 0.14, 108.8, 124.7,
  "SPI/II3s.96h", "12%", 0.9, 0.34, 133.1, 186.6
) |>
  mutate(
    calc1 = 94.9 * exp(beta), calc2 = 94.9 * exp(2 * beta),
    # beta printed to 2 decimals: +/- 0.005 moves CL by up to 0.5% (1 copy)
    # and 1% (2 copies)
    ok = abs(calc1 / cl1 - 1) < 0.0051 & abs(calc2 / cl2 - 1) < 0.0101
  )
s1 |>
  select(scenario, rgc, pct, beta, cl1, calc1, cl2, calc2) |>
  rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "RGC" = rgc, "Percentile" = pct, "beta" = beta,
    "CL, SNP = 1 (Table S1)" = cl1, "CL, SNP = 1 (recomputed)" = calc1,
    "CL, SNP = 2 (Table S1)" = cl2, "CL, SNP = 2 (recomputed)" = calc2
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(s1$ok))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Anonymised drug and units.** The paper names neither the drug nor its
  units. Doses are in "units"; the volumes and clearances are taken to share
  one undisclosed volume unit, and time is in hours (the sampling times). The
  model is registered under the paper's own label, `drugS`.
- **Concentration scale.** The authors' code (Data S1) gives each dose record
  an amount of `1000 x DOSE` and divides by V1, so its simulated
  concentrations, and Supplementary Figure S5, are on a "1000 x units per
  volume" scale (ng/mL if the units are mg and volumes L). The model keeps
  `amt` in units and multiplies by 1000 in `Cc`, which reproduces that scale.
- **IIV magnitudes.** Table 1 headers the IIV column "omega (%)". Data S1 uses
  those numbers directly as the standard deviation of the normal random effect
  (`rnorm(sd = OMEGA)`), and the Methods give `omega2 CL = 0.06` for the
  tabulated 25.1%; so the variances are the squares (0.251^2 = 0.063), not
  `log(CV^2 + 1)`.
- **One random effect on F.** Table 1 prints 32.9% beside both ImaxF and D50F;
  Data S1 has a single `omF` applied to F itself (`F1 = Fpop * exp(ETA_F)`),
  which the model follows. An individual F can exceed 1, as in the source.
- **The 20-unit threshold.** The Table 1 footnote sets F = 1 for doses below
  20 units and uses the Imax form from 20 units; Data S1 uses `<= 20`. Both
  give F = 1 at exactly 20 units.
- **No IIV** on V1, Ka, Tlag2, EmaxFRAC or D50FRAC, as in Table 1 and Data S1.
- **Residual error.** Proportional 20% (`SIG_slope = 0.2`) with no additive
  part (`SIG_inter = 0`).
- **Genetic effects** are not part of the model; see "The pharmacogenetic
  layer" for how to reproduce the H1 and 60% scenarios. The SNP genotypes
  were simulated from HapMap with Hapgen2 and are not reproducible here.
- **Phase II steady state** is reached by a 30-day once-daily run-in, not by
  `ss` flags (see the steady-state section). Only the SPI/II3s.96h design is
  simulated: the sampling times of the two other phase II designs (optimised
  with PFIM) are not printed.
- **Citation.** The article's last page number is not in the source on disk;
  the reference gives the first page only. No correction notice for the
  article was found in Europe PMC as of 2026-11-24.
